page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.126-1008 is a large-scale, general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at 2.7 GHz, delivering 126 physical cores and 252 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. System memory is scaled in a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 1008 GB of total RAM, which equals 4.0 GB of memory per allocated virtual processor.

Hardware allocation is dedicated to the instance, ensuring predictable compute execution across all 252 execution threads. The instance configuration includes zero local storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be handled via external network-attached block volumes. Furthermore, it contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource footprint maximizes execution density on a single node without the overhead of physical hardware management, delivering cost-effective utilization of high-core-count AMD silicon for centralized scaling.

Given its massive core count, high memory capacity, and standard memory-to-core balance, VM.Standard.E6.Flex.126-1008 is designed for compute-intensive enterprise applications. Workload profiles that align with this instance include distributed build systems, large web serving fleets, enterprise resource planning backends, massive parallel batch processing, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency microservice application clusters that rely on remote storage architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.126-1008 is a high-density, general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 126 physical cores across 252 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core, combined with 1008 GB of system memory. Following a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, it sustains high thread concurrency for parallelized tasks. The hardware profile does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU acceleration, requiring data persistence to be handled via attached cloud block storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned by default. By offering high thread and memory density on modern AMD silicon, the server provides cost-efficient scaling for centralized enterprise workloads, including large-scale CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration worker pools, extensive batch processing, ETL data transformations, and high-throughput application serving.
